learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamentals of automatisms and control methods.
Understand the fundamentals of Control Systems and Automation.
Apply the principles of Automation and control to model and analyze dynamic systems.
Analyze the transient and steady-state response of systems and processes.
Able to design and simulate the dynamic behavior of systems and processes in the laboratory.
Able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions, and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.

syllabus_topics: Principles of Automatic Control. Modeling and analysis of dynamic systems. Dynamic behavior of systems.
1. Introduction to control systems and automation.
2. Control systems. Laplace Transform.
2.1. Laplace Transform of typical signals.
2.2. Theorems and properties of the Laplace Transform.
2.3. Inverse Laplace Transform.
3. Automation and control. Mathematical modeling of dynamic systems.
3.1. Introduction.
3.2. Transfer Function.
3.3. Block Diagram.
3.4. Flow Diagram.
4. Automation and control. Dynamic Systems in State Space.
4.1. State Space Modeling.
4.2. Transfer Functions of Some Physical Elements and Systems.
5. Analysis of the transient response of systems and processes.
5.1. 1st order systems, Impulse response, Unit step response, Unit ramp response.
5.2. 2nd order systems, Types of damping, Impulse response, Unit step response, Specifications, Unit ramp response.
5.3. Routh-Hurwitz criterion. Stability of systems and processes.
6. Analysis of the steady-state response of systems and processes.
6.1. Steady-state error.
6.2. Error constants.
6.3. Errors in systems with non-unity feedback.
7. Root Locus.
7.1. Plotting the roots of the characteristic equation.
7.2. Basic equations of the root locus.
7.3. General rules for constructing the root locus.
7.4. Addition of poles and zeros to a second-order system.
8. Analysis of the frequency response of systems and processes.
8.1. Calculation of system gain and phase.
8.2. Bode Diagram.
8.3. Frequency domain specifications.
teaching_methods: Classroom presentation of concepts related to the subjects that make up each topic and problem-solving sessions that allow the student to know how to approach them, as well as other group-based face-to-face sessions such as discussion classes, common sharing, etc.
Laboratory activities of increasing difficulty that allow the student to acquire the ability to achieve autonomy in problem-solving.
Completion of work in small groups.
Personal study, report writing, practical exercises, etc., as independent work by the student or group of students.

assessment_methods.method: Project 1: Automation and control of machines, processes and systems

assessment_rules: For the ordinary exam in June and the extraordinary exam in July: The student will be assessed on the material associated with the two partial exams, which will account for 75% of the final grade. The remaining 25% will correspond to practices, the proposed project, and the evaluation of computerized process management.
